scenes.heading: Rounding and significant figures
scenes.say: Fuel at one dollar eighty-seven point nine a litre. About twenty-six million Australians. A cash total rounded to five cents. All of these are rounding. Let's learn to do it right.
scenes.caption: Fuel at $1.879 a litre. About 26 million Australians. A cash total rounded to 5 cents. All of these are rounding.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Get off at the nearest bus stop
scenes.science: Round to the nearest allowed number, like 3.4 or 3.5
scenes.breaks: A rounded number is only a label, not the true value. Errors grow if you keep using it.
scenes.say: Imagine bus stops every hundred metres. You get dropped at whichever stop is closer, and if you're exactly halfway, you go forward. Rounding is the same: the stops are the numbers you're allowed, and you move to the nearest one. But remember, the rounded number isn't the true value.

scenes.heading: Which is closer?
scenes.say: First the number line from three point four to three point five, in hundredths. Now the dot at three point four seven. It's only three hundredths from three point five, so to one decimal place it rounds to three point five.
scenes.caption: A number line from 3.4 to 3.5. The dot at 3.47 is only 0.03 from 3.5, so to one decimal place it rounds to 3.5.

scenes.heading: Significant figures
points: Start at the first non-zero digit
scenes.say: Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit. Zeros sandwiched between digits count, so three hundred and seven has three. Leading zeros never count, so zero point zero zero four zero six has three too. And keep the size: fifty-eight thousand three hundred and sixty-two to two significant figures is fifty-eight thousand.
scenes.caption: Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit. Sandwich zeros count: 307 has 3 s.f. Leading zeros never count: 0.00406 has 3 s.f. Keep the size: 58 362 to 2 s.f. is 58 000.

scenes.heading: Estimate first
scenes.question: Estimate 48.7 × 0.312 ÷ 9.6.
scenes.say: Estimate forty-eight point seven times point three one two, divided by nine point six. Round each number to one significant figure: fifty, point three and ten. Fifty times point three is fifteen, and fifteen divided by ten is one point five. The calculator gives about one point five eight, so the estimate checks out.
scenes.caption: Estimate 48.7 × 0.312 ÷ 9.6. Round to 1 s.f.: 50 × 0.3 ÷ 10 = 1.5. The calculator gives about 1.58, so the estimate checks out.

scenes.heading: Cash rounding to 5 cents
scenes.say: Australia has no one or two cent coins, so cash totals round to the nearest five cents. One or two cents drop to zero. Three or four jump to five. Six or seven drop to five. Eight or nine jump to ten. So twenty-seven dollars sixty-three in cash becomes twenty-seven sixty-five.
scenes.caption: Cash totals round to the nearest 5 cents. 1 or 2 drop to 0, 3 or 4 jump to 5, 6 or 7 drop to 5, 8 or 9 jump to 10. So $27.63 in cash becomes $27.65.

points: 5 or more, round up; 4 or less, stay
Decimal places count after the point
Sig figs start at first non-zero digit
scenes.say: Quick recap. Five or more rounds up. Decimal places count after the point, and significant figures start at the first non-zero digit. Estimate by rounding to one significant figure. And always round once, at the end. Now try the practice questions!
